Overview

Why early advice matters

Being investigated or charged is stressful, and what happens at the start of a case can shape everything that follows. Taking advice before any interview is important.

We advise at police and council interviews, represent clients in the Magistrates’ Court, and handle Crown Court matters with counsel. We have also worked on prosecutions brought by local authorities, so we understand how these cases are built.

How we can help

  • Advise you before and during interviews
  • Make bail applications and pre-charge representations
  • Represent you in the Magistrates’ Court
  • Instruct counsel for Crown Court matters
  • Advise on and pursue appeals

How we work

What happens next

  1. Step 01

    Contact us early

    Tell us as soon as you are contacted, arrested or invited to an interview.

  2. Step 02

    Advice before interview

    We find out what we can about the allegation and advise you before you answer questions.

  3. Step 03

    Representation

    We prepare your case and represent you, instructing counsel where needed.

  4. Step 04

    Outcome

    We explain the outcome, and any options for appeal.

FAQs

Common questions

I have been invited to a voluntary interview. Do I need a solicitor?

We strongly recommend taking advice before any interview under caution, including a voluntary interview. Contact us as soon as you are invited so we can prepare with you.

What is an interview under caution by a council?

Local authorities investigate and prosecute some offences themselves, for example fly-tipping, Blue Badge fraud and social housing fraud. An interview under caution is a formal interview, and what you say may be used as evidence. Take advice before you attend.

Do you handle Crown Court cases?

Yes. We handle Crown Court matters working with counsel (a barrister).

How much will it cost?

We will discuss costs with you at the outset and confirm them in writing. Published prices for criminal defence are being finalised and will appear on our Fees page.
